To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HES family of Notch effector genes inhibit exocrine differentiation in the embryonic pancreas by binding to Ptf1-p28, a component of the PTF-1 transcription factor complex that promotes exocrine differentiation.
the Notch effector protein Hes1 inhibits the activity of the pancreatic transcription factor, Ptf1a, by direct protein-protein interaction.
Notch signalling delays exocrine pancreatic differentiation by inhibiting activity of the Ptf1 transcriptional complex and that this effect is mediated by direct interaction between Hes1 and Ptf1p48.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the PTF1 and Notch signalling pathways interact to control exocrine differentiation in the developing pancreas.

the mechanisms by which the Notch pathway regulates pancreatic development and differentiation, and defines the interaction between HES proteins and the PTF1-p48 subunit of the PTF-1 transcription factor complex as a critical step in this process.
the molecular basis of the Notch effect on pancreatic differentiation, and suggests a mechanism for the regulation of PTF1 complex function during development and disease
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ptf1-p4 interaction is a key mechanism in the regulation of exocrine pancreatic differentiation.
the Hes1 and Ptf1a proteins interact directly to modulate the transcriptional activity of Ptf1a.
HES1, HES5 and HEY1 are able to bind to Ptf1-p4 and inhibit the PTF1 activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Notch pathway regulates exocrine pancreas differentiation by inhibiting the PTF1 activity through the interaction of HES family members with the PTF1-p48 subunit.
Ptf1-p58 is a target of the Notch signaling pathway, which is consistent with previous reports that the Notch pathway inhibits pancreatic exocrine differentiation.
the Hes family of bHLHe factors interact with Ptf-p48 to repress Ptf1-p50-mediated gene expression.
